title: Celestial equator above Paranal
caption: Star trails at the celestial equator above Paranal Observatory, Chile
celestial: Photograph taken at Paranal Observatory, Chile

recognition.text: Published in the ESO image archive. No published rating.

story: Stars leave trails across the sky over Paranal, and the telescopes below appear blurred. Both effects come from the long exposure time used to take the picture: the telescopes were turning while the camera collected light, and so was the sky.

The photograph is framed with the celestial equator in the middle. That is the line in the sky directly above Earth's equator. Along it, the star trails run straight. Move away from it on either side, and the trails begin to bend into circles, one set curving around the northern celestial pole and the other around the southern one.

This makes the picture a neat demonstration of how the sky seems to move. Earth spins on its axis, so every star appears to circle one of the two celestial poles. Stars near a pole trace tight circles, while those at the equator trace the widest paths of all, which look like straight lines in a photo.

understand.summary: This is a long-exposure landscape photograph taken in visible light with a camera at Paranal. The exposure settings and colour processing are not published.
understand.eye: The eye would see sharp points of starlight and still telescopes; only a long exposure turns the stars into trails and blurs the moving telescopes.

explore: The caption notes that the telescopes themselves were rotating during the exposure, which is why they appear blurred. The star trails and the blurred telescopes both come from the same long exposure.
alt: Star trails running straight across the centre of the sky and curving on either side above blurred telescope enclosures.
